newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says '97 record for pipelines.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says '97 record for pipelines.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it planned to lay 900 km (560 miles) of submarine gas pipeline in 1997, more than in any previous year.

The world's longest subsea pipeline, NorFra -- running from the North Sea Draupner E riser platform to a receiving terminal at Dunkerque in France, accounts for almost 830 km and will be laid from two laybarges (LB).
In addition, the company will lay more than 60 km remaining to complete the Zeepipe IIB, according to Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter.

LB200 will be in position this week to resume laying Zeepipe IIB, which runs from Draupner E to Kollsnes near Bergen on the west coast of Norway. Statoil said the work should take about one month depending on weather conditions.
"If everything goes to plan, LB200 can start laying NorFra southwards from Draupner E in the first half of April," it said.

At the same time, a second barge, DLB1601, will begin on the southern section of NorFra, which will run southwards for 280 km from a point on the Dutch continental shelf to the inshore zone off the Dunkerque landfall.
Including the inshore and land sections in France, NorFra will be 840 km long.
